phinehas.about: High Priest living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
phinehas.note: Aaron's grandson, Eleazar's son. When Israel was being struck by a plague for idolatry and sexual sin with Moabite women, Phinehas drove a spear through an Israelite man and a Midianite woman together, and the plague stopped.

piram.title: Piram
piram.note: King of Jarmuth, one of five Amorite kings who besieged Gibeon. Joshua beat them in the battle where the sun stood still, and the five were found hiding in a cave at Makkedah.

pisgah.title: Pisgah
pisgah.note: Moses looked out over the promised land from the top of Pisgah before he died. Balak had brought Balaam up the same ridge in Moab to curse Israel's camp. It belongs to the range called Abarim.

rabbah.title: Rabbah
rabbah.note: Capital of Ammon. David's army besieged it, and Uriah died in that siege, put where the fighting was worst on David's orders.

rabbith.title: Rabbith
rabbith.note: A border town of Issachar, named once in Joshua 19:20, and nobody knows its site.

rahab.title: Rahab
rahab.note: A prostitute in Jericho. She hid the two spies Joshua sent ahead, and for that, and for the faith she declared in Israel's God, she and her family were spared when the city fell.

rakkath.title: Rakkath
rakkath.note: Naphtali's fortified town on the shore of the Sea of Galilee. Jewish tradition says Herod Antipas later built Tiberias on top of it.

rakkon.title: Rakkon
rakkon.note: On the coast north of Joppa, near the mouth of the Yarkon, this town belonged to Dan. It is generally placed at Tell er-Reqqeit.

ramah.title: Ramah
ramah.note: Samuel's hometown, and where he was buried. The name was common enough that several towns carried it. Jeremiah's Rachel weeping for her children is set here too.

ramah-2.title: Ramah
ramah-2.note: Named once, in Joshua, and nowhere else.

ramah-3.title: Ramah
ramah-3.note: Joshua names him once, and nothing else is recorded.

ramoth.title: Ramoth
ramoth.note: Ramoth in Gilead, one of the cities of refuge east of the Jordan. Israel and Aram fought over it again and again. Ahab took his death wound there in disguise, and later Jehu was anointed king in the same place.

reba.title: Reba
reba.about: King living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
reba.note: One of five Midianite kings killed in the war Moses ordered shortly before his death. His land was later counted in Reuben's share. Joshua 13:21 lists him again with the others.

rehob.title: Rehob
rehob.note: The far edge of the spies' route into Canaan, up in the north. Asher was allotted a Rehob too, and Judges 1:31 says Asher never drove out the people living there.

rehob-3.title: Rehob
rehob-3.note: Joshua names him once, and nothing else is recorded.

rekem-3.title: Rekem
rekem-3.note: Joshua names him once, and nothing else is recorded.

rekem.title: Rekem
rekem.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
rekem.note: One of the five Midianite kings Israel killed in the days of Moses. The same name belongs to a man in Manasseh's genealogy.

remeth-2.title: Remeth
remeth-2.note: A town of Issachar in Joshua's allotment list. It is probably the town listed elsewhere as Ramoth and Jarmuth.

remmon-4.title: Remmon
remmon-4.note: Named twice, in Joshua and 1 Chronicles, and nowhere else.

remmon-3.title: Remmon
remmon-3.note: A town in the far south, named in the town lists of Joshua 15:32 and 19:7 and again in 1 Chronicles 4:32.

reuben.title: Reuben
reuben.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
reuben.note: Jacob's firstborn. He slept with one of his father's concubines and lost the birthright for it, and Jacob had not forgotten it on his deathbed.

rumah-2.title: Rumah
rumah-2.note: A town in the hill-country list of Judah (Joshua 15:52), and its site is uncertain.

salcah.title: Salcah
salcah.note: The eastern edge of Israelite settlement. Salcah was a city of Bashan, given to the half tribe of Manasseh once Og, king of Bashan, was beaten.

sansannah.title: Sansannah
sansannah.note: A town in the Negev of Judah. Joshua 19:5 calls it Hazar-susah and 1 Chronicles 4:31 calls it Hazar-susim, and the names mean roughly village of the horse.

sarid.title: Sarid
sarid.note: On Zebulun's border, west of Chisloth-tabor. Nobody has pinned down the site, though several ruins in the eastern Jezreel valley have been put forward.

secacah.title: Secacah
secacah.note: In Judah's wilderness district on the western shore of the Dead Sea, one of six towns listed with Beth-arabah, Middin and En-gedi. Its exact site is unknown.

seir.title: Seir
seir.note: A rough range of mountains east of the Arabah. It runs from the bottom of the Dead Sea toward the Gulf of Aqabah. The Horites lived there first, and Esau's descendants pushed them out.

shaalabbin.title: Shaalabbin
shaalabbin.note: Allotted to Dan, but the Danites never fully took it, and Amorites held on there until they were put to forced labour. It is also spelled Shaalbim.

shaaraim.title: Shaaraim
shaaraim.note: The name means two gates. When David killed Goliath, the Philistines fled along the road past this Shaaraim, out in the Shephelah.

shahazimah.title: Shahazimah
shahazimah.note: A border town of Issachar. The name means toward the heights, and nobody knows where it was.

shamir-3.title: Shamir
shamir-3.note: Named once, in Joshua, and nowhere else.

sharuhen-2.title: Sharuhen
sharuhen-2.note: A town of Simeon inside Judah's land, called Shaaraim in 1 Chronicles 4:31. Egyptian records describe a fortress by this name that the Hyksos held.

sheba-2.title: Sheba
sheba-2.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
sheba-2.note: He raised a revolt against David in 2 Samuel 20 and called the northern tribes away from him. It ended at a walled town, with his head thrown over the wall to the men outside.

shebam.title: Shebam
shebam.note: Good grazing land east of the Jordan, taken from Sihon, which Reuben and Gad asked for because of their flocks.

shebarim.title: Shebarim
shebarim.note: Israel's first attack on Ai failed, and the men ran. They were chased down the slope as far as Shebarim, and the defeat was later traced to Achan's sin.

shechem.title: Shechem
shechem.note: Abram stopped here when he first came into the land, and Joseph's brothers were grazing the flocks near it when Joseph went looking for them. The city took its name from a Canaanite prince.

shechem-3.title: Shechem
shechem-3.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
shechem-3.note: A different Shechem from the prince, named in the clan lists at Numbers 26:31 and Joshua 17:2.

shema-4.title: Shema
shema-4.note: A town of Judah in the Negev, among the southernmost cities near the border of Edom. It is generally identified with the Sheba of Joshua 19:2.

shemida.title: Shemida
shemida.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
shemida.note: Gilead's son and Manasseh's great-grandson, and his descendants made one of the clans of Manasseh.

sheshai.title: Sheshai
sheshai.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
sheshai.note: One of the sons of Anak. Caleb drove him out of Hebron when he finally claimed the land promised to him decades earlier.

shicron.title: Shicron
shicron.note: A landmark on Judah's northern border, between Ekron and Jabneel near the coast. Nothing else is recorded of it, and the site is unknown.

shihon.title: Shihon
shihon.note: A town of Issachar, named only in Joshua 19:19, and still not found.

shihor.title: Shihor
shihor.note: The stream on Egypt's northeastern border. It marks the southwestern edge of the land promised to Israel.

shihor-libnath.title: Shihor-libnath
shihor-libnath.note: Not a person but a stream on the southern boundary of Asher. It is generally identified with the Nahr Zarqa, which rises in the Carmel range.

shilhim.title: Shilhim
shilhim.note: A town in the south of Judah, near the border with Simeon. It is generally identified with the Sharuhen of Joshua 19:6, which Egyptian sources know as a fortress.

shiloh.title: Shiloh
shiloh.note: The tabernacle stood at Shiloh, north of Bethel in Ephraim, for most of the time of the judges. Young Samuel served there. After the Philistines captured the ark, the place faded.

shimon-meron.title: Shimon-meron
shimon-meron.note: Joshua beat thirty-one kings west of the Jordan, and the king of Shimon-meron was one of them. It is generally taken to be the same place as Shimron.

shimron-2.title: Shimron
shimron-2.note: Named twice, in Joshua, and nowhere else.

shinar.title: Shinar
shinar.note: The old name for the land of Babylon. The tower of Babel went up there, and much later it was the heart of Nebuchadnezzar's empire.

shittim.title: Shittim
shittim.note: Israel's last camp before crossing into Canaan, on the plain of Moab across from Jericho. It was there that the men were drawn into idolatry with Moabite women.

shocho.title: Shocho
shocho.note: A town of Judah near the Valley of Elah, close to where David fought Goliath.

shocho-3.title: Shocho
shocho-3.note: Named once, in Joshua, and nowhere else.

shunem.title: Shunem
shunem.note: A village of Issachar near Jezreel. The Philistines camped here before the battle on Mount Gilboa where Saul and his sons died, and a woman here built a room for Elisha.

sidon.title: Sidon
sidon.note: The older of the two great Phoenician ports, north of Tyre. It was allotted to Asher, but Asher never took it.

sihon.title: Sihon
sihon.about: King living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
sihon.note: An Amorite king. Israel asked to pass through his land, and he attacked them instead. It cost him his kingdom east of the Jordan.

simeon.title: Simeon
simeon.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
simeon.note: Jacob's second son. With his brother Levi he killed the men of Shechem after their sister Dinah was raped. Jacob held it against them on his deathbed.

succoth.title: Succoth
succoth.note: Jacob built shelters for his cattle here, east of the Jordan near the Jabbok, on his way back from Paddan-aram. The name means booths.

taanach.title: Taanach
taanach.note: A Canaanite royal city on the southwest edge of the Jezreel Valley, near Megiddo. Joshua beat its king, the town went to the Levites of Kohath, and its Canaanites were never driven out. Deborah's song puts a battle there by the waters of Megiddo.

taanath-shiloh.title: Taanath-shiloh
taanath-shiloh.note: A point on Ephraim's southern border, named once in Joshua 16:6. The name seems to mean approach to Shiloh, and it is commonly identified with the ruin of Ta'na southeast of Shechem.

tabor.title: Tabor
tabor.note: A dome-shaped mountain rising out of the Jezreel Valley, on the line between Zebulun and Issachar. Deborah sent Barak there to gather Israel before the battle with Sisera. The psalmist sets it beside Hermon, and Hosea and Jeremiah both name it in oracles of judgment.

talmai-2.title: Talmai
talmai-2.about: King living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
talmai-2.note: Caleb drove three Anakim giants out of Hebron, and Talmai was one of them.

tappuah.title: Tappuah
tappuah.note: A town on the line between Ephraim and Manasseh.

tappuah-3.title: Tappuah
tappuah-3.note: Named once, in Joshua, and nowhere else.

tarah.title: Tarah
tarah.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
tarah.note: Abraham's father, whose family line Genesis 11 traces. Joshua 24:2 names him again.

taralah.title: Taralah
taralah.note: A town given to Benjamin, in the hill country near Gibeon. Nobody has found the site.

telem-2.title: Telem
telem-2.note: A town on Judah's southern border, in the list at Joshua 15:24. It may be the Telaim where Saul gathered his army against the Amalekites.

timnah.title: Timnah
timnah.note: The Philistine town where Samson saw the woman he wanted to marry. The riddle at that wedding feast started his long fight with the Philistines.

timnah-2.title: Timnah
timnah-2.note: Named once, in Joshua, and nowhere else.

timnath-heres.title: Timnath-heres
timnath-heres.note: The name means portion of the sun. Joshua was given this town in the hill country of Ephraim and was buried there, north of the hill of Gaash. The book of Joshua spells it Timnath-serah.

tirzah.title: Tirzah
tirzah.note: An old Canaanite royal city that served as capital of the northern kingdom before Samaria was built. The Song of Solomon sets its beauty beside Jerusalem's. Menahem seized the throne from there.

tirzah-2.title: Tirzah
tirzah-2.about: Woman living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
tirzah-2.note: She was the youngest of Zelophehad's five daughters, named with her sisters each time the family's inheritance comes up.

tyre.title: Tyre
tyre.note: The leading Phoenician port, partly on the mainland and partly on an island offshore, rich from sea trade and purple dye made from murex shells. Its king Hiram sent cedar and craftsmen for David and Solomon. The prophets attacked its pride and said it would fall.

ummah.title: Ummah
ummah.note: One of Asher's towns in Joshua 19:30. Some Greek manuscripts read Acco here, and many scholars prefer that, since Acco is otherwise missing from Asher's list.

zaannannim.title: Zaannannim
zaannannim.note: On Naphtali's border, near Kedesh, by the oak where Heber the Kenite had his tent. Sisera ran there after his army broke at the Kishon, and Heber's wife Jael killed him.

zabdi.title: Zabdi
zabdi.note: Achan's grandfather. When Joshua went looking for who had taken the plunder from Jericho, the lot came down through his household.

zanoah.title: Zanoah
zanoah.note: A town in Judah. Its people repaired one of Jerusalem's gates when Nehemiah rebuilt the walls.

zanoah-2.title: Zanoah
zanoah-2.note: Named once, in Joshua, and nowhere else.

zaphon.title: Zaphon
zaphon.note: The name means north, and it was a town of Gad in the Jordan Valley. Some scholars find it again in Judges 12:1, where the Ephraimites gather to confront Jephthah. Nobody has located it.

zarah.title: Zarah
zarah.about: Judah's son living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
zarah.note: Judah's son by Tamar, Perez's twin. His hand came out first and the midwife tied a scarlet thread on it, and then Perez was born ahead of him.

zarchite.title: Zarchite
zarchite.about: Judah's son living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
zarchite.note: A descendant of Zerah. It shows up in the census lists and the rosters in Chronicles and never attaches to anyone well known.

zareah.title: Zareah
zareah.note: Samson's hometown, better known as Zorah, on the border of Judah and Dan. The angel of the Lord told Manoah's wife there that she would have a son, and Samson was buried between Zorah and Eshtaol.

zareth-shahar.title: Zareth-shahar
zareth-shahar.note: Splendor of the dawn. It was a town of Reuben on a hill above the plain by the Dead Sea, usually placed near the mouth of the Wadi Zarqa Ma'in.

zarthan.title: Zarthan
zarthan.note: The Jordan's waters piled up near Zarthan when Israel crossed on dry ground. Centuries later Solomon's bronze for the temple was cast in the clay ground between Succoth and Zarthan. Exactly where in the plain it stood is uncertain.

zebulun.title: Zebulun
zebulun.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
zebulun.note: Jacob's tenth son and Leah's last. His tribe's land ran up to the Sea of Galilee, and Isaiah names it with Naphtali as the place where a light would dawn, which Matthew applies to Jesus in Galilee.

zelah.title: Zelah
zelah.note: A town of Benjamin, probably Saul's own. David had the bones of Saul and Jonathan brought back and buried there in the tomb of Kish.

zelophehad.title: Zelophehad
zelophehad.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
zelophehad.note: He died in the wilderness with five daughters and no sons. They went to Moses and asked for their father's land, and they got it, and the law of inheritance changed because of them.

zemaraim.title: Zemaraim
zemaraim.note: Two places. One is a town of Benjamin, generally put at a ruin north of Jericho. The other is a hill in Ephraim where Abijah of Judah beat Jeroboam's much bigger army.

zenan.title: Zenan
zenan.note: A lowland town of Judah. Micah probably means the same place when he says Zaanan's people will not come out, and nobody has found the site.

zer.title: Zer
zer.note: It was a walled town of Naphtali, probably near the southwest shore of the Sea of Galilee, exact site unknown.

ziddim.title: Ziddim
ziddim.note: A walled town of Naphtali, listed with Hazor, Rakkath and Kinnereth. Some place it near the Sea of Galilee.

ziklag.title: Ziklag
ziklag.note: Achish of Gath gave this town in the Negev to David while he was running from Saul, and David lived there more than a year. Amalekites burned it while he was away and took the women and children, and he went after them and got everyone back.

zin.title: Zin
zin.note: The Wilderness of Zin, where Kadesh lay. Miriam died there, and there Moses struck the rock in anger when he had been told to speak to it.

zior.title: Zior
zior.note: In the hill country of Judah near Hebron, named once, and commonly identified with es-Sa'ir northeast of Hebron.

ziph.title: Ziph
ziph.note: David hid in the wilderness around Ziph, southeast of Hebron, while Saul was hunting him. The people of Ziph told Saul where he was, twice.

ziph-3.title: Ziph
ziph-3.note: Named once, in Joshua, and nowhere else.

zippor.title: Zippor
zippor.about: Moabite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
zippor.note: Balak's father. Balak was the Moabite king who hired Balaam to curse Israel.

zur-2.title: Zur
zur-2.about: King living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
zur-2.note: A Midianite chief killed in Israel's war against Midian. Phinehas had already killed his daughter Cozbi over the idolatry that brought the plague.
